paper: Xie & Nagaosa, arXiv:2504.14166 (iCDW loop-current collective modes)

open_questions.question: What sets the magnitude of the NV-detectable stray field and the resulting T1 relaxation time (Eqs. 13-15), which we did not attempt?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The whole experimental proposal hinges on whether the phason-driven dynamic flux produces magnetic noise above the NV sensitivity floor; the theory paper gives only a qualitative Fermi-golden-rule estimate.
open_questions.next_step: Compute delta-Phi from the excited A1 phason amplitude, propagate the Biot-Savart stray field to a realistic NV standoff (10-100 nm), and evaluate S_B(omega0) and T1 for AV3Sb5 loop-current magnitudes from DFT/experiment.

open_questions.question: How does the mode-mixing signature evolve at finite q (dispersion), beyond the q=0 M-point result we reproduced?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Real spectroscopy (IXS, Raman, pump-probe) probes finite-q; the kappa1 q^2 gradient terms shift the mixed-mode dispersions and could change the mode ordering shown schematically in Fig. 3(b).
open_questions.next_step: Diagonalize the full q-dependent Eq.(10) matrix over the folded BZ using a fitted kappa1, and map the avoided-crossing / mixing strength as a function of q.

open_questions.question: Does the mode mixing survive coupling to itinerant electrons (Landau damping) near the Van Hove filling?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper's modes are from a phenomenological Lagrangian; at the VHS the CDW couples strongly to particle-hole continua, which can damp/broaden the Higgs and shift the phason gap.
open_questions.next_step: Compute the electronic polarization bubble Pi(q,omega) at 5/12 filling on the kagome lattice and dress the fluctuation propagator (RPA) to check whether the A-channel mixing peak remains a sharp resonance.

open_questions.question: How robust is the iCDW-vs-rCDW selection (sign of b) to the third-order lambda3 term we set to zero (following ref. 13)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The lambda3 cos(theta1)cos(theta2)cos(theta3) term, dropped by convention, can compete with lambda2 and alter the phase selection and hence whether sin(3 theta0) is nonzero.
open_questions.next_step: Reintroduce lambda3 and re-minimize F over the full (theta1,theta2,theta3) space (no C3 assumption) to map the phase boundary and confirm iCDW stability window.

open_questions.question: Can the microscopic kernel be made self-consistent so the loop-current order emerges spontaneously rather than as a linear response to an imposed flux?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Our cross-check imposes an external Peierls flux; a genuine iCDW requires the loop current to be self-generated by interactions, tying the phenomenological |Delta_Q| to a microscopic order parameter.
open_questions.next_step: Add a mean-field imaginary bond order decoupling (V * <i c_i^dag c_j>) to the kagome kernel and iterate to self-consistency at VHS filling to obtain a spontaneous loop-current solution.

next_steps: Extend the q=0 replication to the full finite-q dispersion over the folded BZ.
Attempt a quantitative NV T1/stray-field estimate with realistic AV3Sb5 parameters.
Dress fluctuation modes with the electronic polarization bubble (RPA) at VHS filling.
Reintroduce lambda3 and relax the C3 constraint to test phase-selection robustness.
Make the microscopic loop-current kernel self-consistent for spontaneous iCDW order.
